---
title: "Releases"
---

The data is never committed to the repository: the corpora live in four
GitHub releases.

| Release | Content | Keyed by |
|---|---|---|
| `scjn-leyes` | 315 federal laws, reform-dated snapshots | `abrev` (the slug) |
| `scjn-reglamentos` | federal *reglamentos* | `id_ordenamiento` |
| `scjn-lineamientos` | federal *lineamientos* | `id_ordenamiento` |
| `scjn-tratados` | international treaties | `id_ordenamiento` |

Each release carries an index plus one tarball per instrument. An instrument
with no consolidated text is indexed with `snapshots: 0` and has no tarball;
reading it raises `SinTextoEnSCJN`.

## A release is a series

A GitHub release holds at most 1,000 assets, so a release is a series of tags:
a part keeps the bare tag (`scjn-tratados`) and a continuation adds `-<n>`
(`scjn-tratados-2`, `-3`, ...). The reader asks GitHub for the bare tag and then
probes `-1`, `-2`, ... until one answers 404.

## Where the releases live

The four releases live in this repository,
[`legistlan/scjn`](https://github.com/legistlan/scjn/releases), and that is the
repository `scjn.release.release_repository()` names by default.
Set the environment variable `SCJN_RELEASE_REPOSITORY` (`<owner>/<name>`) to
point every lookup at a mirror of the releases elsewhere; it is read on every
call, so one process can be pointed elsewhere without reloading anything. The `gh` commands
that the packaging scripts print in `PUBLICAR.md` follow the same variable.

## Nothing is published automatically

No workflow publishes SCJN-derived data. The SCJN's search can return a
completely wrong document for an instrument, so a human decides what is safe to
publish. Every packaging script writes a `PUBLICAR.md` and uploads nothing; a
regenerated release is replaced in place (same tag, `--clobber`). See
[Crawl](crawl.qmd).

## Reading a release

[Command line](cli.qmd) puts a release on disk, and [Python](python.qmd) reads
it. Every reader is disk-first: it reads the cache and raises `AssetNotCached`
for anything not there.
